whatItDoes: Inference Labs' Proof-of-Inference subnet: builds zk-ML verification so an AI prediction can be proven to come from a specific model. Miners produce verifiable predictions plus zero-knowledge proofs; validators verify proofs and score them. It earns by supplying verifiable-inference infrastructure - trust-minimized AI outputs for buyers who cannot trust a black-box API.
hardwareRec: CPU-only per README: 8-core 3.2GHz+ (3.6GHz+ competitive), 32-64GB RAM, 400Mbps-1Gbps symmetric network, 1-2TB NVMe SSD. zk-proving is CPU-heavy; faster CPU/network/storage directly raises rewards. Rented cloud VMs are fine; no GPU required.
keyRequirements: Run the sn2-miner Rust binary (prebuilt release, Docker image, or build from source)
Registered hotkey on netuid 2 (finney); PM2 or Docker+watchtower recommended
Score = cryptographic integrity, time-to-proof, proof size, and response time
Binaries auto-update every 5 minutes with atomic replacement - do not fight it
HTTP (port 8091) and QUIC (btlightning) endpoints reachable
minerJob: Runs the sn2-miner Rust daemon over HTTP/QUIC. Validators push input data; the miner runs its custom verifiable model - an AI model compiled into a zero-knowledge circuit - and returns the prediction plus a zk proof. Validators verify proofs via the Expander backend and weight miners on proof size, generation time, and response latency. Rewards flow purely from Yuma weights on those performance metrics, so better proving hardware and efficiency mean higher weight. Prebuilt binaries self-update every 5 minutes.
minerJobProvide: Verified AI predictions returned to validator requests
A zero-knowledge proof of inference per prediction (Expander-compatible)
Fast time-to-proof (scored directly)
Compact proofs (proof size is scored)
High-uptime HTTP and QUIC endpoints
top10Strategy: This is a systems/efficiency race, not a model-quality race: winners minimize proof time, proof size, and response latency on strong bare-metal CPUs and 1Gbps+ links. A newcomer breaks top-10 by over-provisioning CPU clock, NVMe, and network, keeping the binary current via auto-update, and watching the stats dashboard to see where the proof-latency frontier sits - every performance point is scored.
top10Levers: CPU clock speed and core count for faster proving
1Gbps+ symmetric network to cut response latency
64GB+ RAM and NVMe storage headroom
Always-current binaries (auto-update channel)
Track sn2-stats.inferencelabs.com and wandb for frontier metrics
followTopMiners: Watch taostats.io/subnet/2 top UIDs and incentive spread, the sn2-stats.inferencelabs.com dashboard and wandb.ai/inferencelabs/subnet-2 for proof-latency distributions, and GitHub release cadence on inference-labs-inc/subnet-2.

whatItDoes: Vanta Network (formerly Taoshi's Proprietary Trading Network): miners submit LONG/SHORT/FLAT futures trade signals across forex, crypto, equities, and commodities (Hyperliquid perps included). Validators simulate fills with fees and slippage, track each miner's equity, and pay weekly PnL-ranked emissions. External traders and the dashboard consume the signals; top miners receive funding via Vanta programs.
hardwareRec: CPU only. Signal submission is strategy logic, not compute-bound; a small VPS (2-4 cores, 8GB RAM) suffices. Real costs are strategy R&D and registration burns; rented GPUs are pointless here.
keyRequirements: Submit orders during market hours per asset class (crypto 24/7, forex Sun 17:00-Fri 17:00 ET, equities 09:30-16:00 ET)
Never exceed 5% intraday or 8% end-of-day drawdown from high-water mark - instant elimination
No plagiarism: copied orders trigger elimination
Each registration needs a fresh unused hotkey; eliminated hotkeys are permanently blacklisted
Carry fees (10.95%/3% per year), spread fees (0.03% crypto, 0.01% equities, 0.005% commodities) and slippage apply
Rank below 25th in your asset class starts a 90-day probation
minerJob: Runs a miner daemon that submits directional orders with entries/exits to validators during market hours. Validators validate trades, simulate portfolio returns with carry fees, spread fees, and leverage-scaled slippage, and continuously track equity against drawdown limits. Weights follow the previous week's PnL scaled by penalties under a debt-based scoring system, with payout periods ending Sunday 00:00 UTC. Elimination is effectively permanent: blacklisted hotkeys cannot re-register, so read docs/miner.md before starting.
minerJobProvide: Timely LONG/SHORT/FLAT signals per supported trade pair
Consistent positive PnL with controlled drawdown
Unique, non-plagiarized order flow
Continuous activity (no 60-day order gaps)
Risk discipline within intraday and EOD drawdown limits
top10Strategy: A zero-sum trading arena where top miners are genuine quant/ML shops. Survive first: small size, strict intraday risk, no leverage spikes; then compound one backtested edge across many pairs to smooth weekly PnL - weights pay last week's PnL net of penalties, so consistency beats home runs. Use the dashboard and Vanta Trading Discord's open strategy resources; expect eliminations while you iterate.
top10Levers: Backtested, unique strategy with positive expectancy across pairs
Hard risk limits - drawdown control is survival
Diversification across asset classes (each class ranks separately)
Minimize carry/spread/slippage drag (low leverage, shorter holds)
Weekly PnL consistency over single lucky trades
followTopMiners: Track the vantanetwork.io dashboard top traders and their return/drawdown profiles, taostats.io/subnet/8 incentive distribution, and docs/miner.md plus the Vanta Trading Discord for rule changes (fees, pairs, drawdown thresholds).

whatItDoes: Cacheon is an inference-speed competition built around SGLang: the validator owns the model, workload, and engine, and miners submit inspectable optimizations - served-model modules or the scheduler's prefix cache - that must measurably speed up end-to-end serving without quality loss. LLM operators benefit from faster/cheaper serving; rewards flow only to measured, qualified improvements.
hardwareRec: Platform data: B300-class GPU (1). Mining itself is code optimization: a local dev GPU to profile SGLang helps, but qualification runs on validator-owned no-egress OCI workers. Software is pre-release; expect policy churn.
keyRequirements: Submit one optimization against a validator-published arena target (forward_pass modules or prefix cache)
Must beat the arena incumbent by the required margin after one complete audited qualification PASS
Stay within behavior and quality limits - speed alone earns nothing
Possible TAO anti-spam admission gate paid to subnet owner (--pay locks the quote ~300 blocks)
Python 3.11+; run cacheon.cli scan/verify locally before submitting
minerJob: Not a 24/7 service. Miners study the validator-published arena, engineer an optimization (engine module or prefix-cache change), run local scan/verify checks, then commit and submit the bundle. The validator builds and runs the candidate in isolated no-egress workers, measures end-to-end latency on the registered agent workload under its speed/quality policy, and records a crown plus V1 credit only if the incumbent is beaten by the required margin. A publisher later combines eligible claims into an on-chain weight vector.
minerJobProvide: Inspectable optimization code for a registered engine target
Measured end-to-end latency improvement over the incumbent
Preserved output quality within policy limits
Passing audited qualification (node audit + graph checks)
Occasional new crown for the target
top10Strategy: A kernel/systems-engineering game: read the docs (concepts, architecture, slot contract), pick one hot target, and profile the SGLang path locally before submitting - blind micro-tweaks waste the admission gate. Because reward requires beating the incumbent on the validator's own benchmark, submissions from engineers with real CUDA/SGLang skill can win fast; the pool of qualified optimizations is tiny and pre-release means early movers shape targets.
top10Levers: Deep SGLang/CUDA optimization skill
Local profiling harness reproducing the registered workload
Target selection where the incumbent is weak
Submit only strong candidates (admission gate economics)
Follow repo commit cadence for fast-moving policy changes
followTopMiners: Watch cacheon.ai/docs (rendered repo docs) and the latent-to/cacheon commit cadence since this is pre-release, plus taostats.io/subnet/14 for weight distribution and which UIDs hold crowns in validator publications.

whatItDoes: SN21 (ippcteam) is a verifiable prediction market for Google Ads campaign outcomes. An operator publishes daily baskets of real account changes (budget/bid changes, pauses); miner containers predict P10/P50/P90 outcome distributions at 7/14/28-day horizons; settled results feed standings that drive emissions. Ad-tech buyers get calibrated forecasts of campaign impact.
hardwareRec: CPU only: 2 cores/4GB min, 4 cores/8GB+ recommended, 20GB SSD. GPU optional for heavier models. Container must run deterministic, network-isolated, under RAM/time budgets.
keyRequirements: Ship a digest-pinned container: stdin episodes to stdout P10/P50/P90 per horizon (7/14/28d)
Commit sn21-model:v1:<repo>@sha256:<digest> on chain; the subnet pulls and runs it daily
Emissions: 1st place 50%, 2nd 25%, 3rd 10% of pot, geometric tail, hard cap 20 earners
250 weighted predictions to place; full standing at 1,000
Score: pinball 50%, interval coverage 10%, direction 15%, goal metric; 12-day half-life standing
Horizon weights: 7d 20%, 14d 35%, 28d 45%
minerJob: Build a forecasting model, package it as a digest-pinned container implementing the MINER_MODEL_SPEC I/O contract, and commit its digest on chain once. Each day the subnet runs your container (network=none, budgeted) against a fresh basket of Google Ads episodes; it emits probabilistic deltas per horizon. Outcomes settle at day 15/22/36; scores roll into a 12-day half-life standing that a published rank curve maps to chain weights. You never POST daily predictions - the container is the miner.
minerJobProvide: Deterministic container emitting calibrated P10/P50/P90 forecasts
Calibration (interval coverage), not just point accuracy
Direction accuracy on the goal metric
Long-horizon stability (28d carries 45% weight)
Maintained on-chain digest commitment
top10Strategy: The rank curve is brutally top-heavy (50/25/10), so top-10 means out-calibrating everyone on quantile accuracy. Start from the docs' training pipeline, backtest against published receipts with verify_day.py, and optimize pinball loss plus coverage before adding complexity. Placement needs 250 weighted predictions and standings decay with a 12-day half-life, so ship early and iterate continuously; a genuinely calibrated simple model beats a fancy miscalibrated one.
top10Levers: Pinball-loss optimization across P10/P50/P90 quantiles
Interval coverage tuning (10% of score)
Horizon-aware training (28d weight 45%)
Early, consistent submission to accumulate standing
Local score reproduction via verify_day.py receipts
followTopMiners: Track the public accuracy/receipt feeds and standings (docs/SN21_VERIFYING.md), taostats.io/subnet/21 weights, and repo docs SN21_REWARDS.md and SN21_STAKING.md - the published feeds mirror the operator's scored record.

whatItDoes: Orion (SILX Labs) is a data-mining subnet: campaigns (currently coding, math, technical, and general-knowledge data for the Quasar model) define what a model needs; miners turn assigned source batches into model-ready datasets and upload signed snapshots. Validators replay a hidden sample to verify, and pay only valid, useful, non-duplicate work. Quasar is the first consumer.
hardwareRec: One modest GPU to run the campaign-pinned Quasar-Preview model locally (--devices 0), plus CPU/RAM for data processing. Needs a Chutes API key and Python 3.11-3.13 with uv. Rented cloud GPUs work.
keyRequirements: Python 3.11-3.13 + uv; install locked deps with uv run --frozen
Chutes API key for the campaign-pinned hosted judge
Process assigned real batches (not individual records) into model-ready datasets
Upload one signed dataset snapshot per assignment to the S3 bucket/prefix
Rewards = verified quality x useful token volume x signed availability history
Invalid, duplicated, stale, or unverifiable work scores zero
minerJob: Run the Orion miner CLI: it picks up signed campaigns and assignments, downloads assigned source data, processes it into model-ready dataset batches, compares the hosted judge against the locally-run Quasar-Preview revision (auto-downloaded from Hugging Face and cached), and uploads one signed snapshot. Validators independently replay a hidden sample, score verified quality and useful token volume, multiply by your signed availability history, and set weights. Availability is a direct reward multiplier, so uptime compounds.
minerJobProvide: Model-ready dataset snapshots per campaign assignment
Signed uploads that survive hidden-sample replay
Local Quasar-Preview runs matching the pinned revision
Sustained signed availability history
Zero duplication or staleness in submissions
top10Strategy: Rewards are quality x volume x availability, so top-10 means high throughput of verified-good data with near-perfect uptime. Automate the whole loop (assignment pickup, processing, judge comparison, signed upload), invest in processing quality over raw volume, and never let the miner go offline - availability multiplies everything. Deduplicate aggressively: stale or duplicate work pays zero and can poison your record.
top10Levers: Uptime and availability history (direct multiplier)
Dataset quality that survives hidden-sample replay
Processing throughput on real assigned batches
Clean dedup and freshness discipline
Right-sized GPU so Quasar-Preview inference stays fast
followTopMiners: Watch taostats.io/subnet/27 weight distribution and per-UID earnings, SILX-LABS/Orion commit cadence (campaign mechanics evolve), and Hugging Face silx-ai Quasar releases since your local model must match the pinned revision.

whatItDoes: Epago is an adversarial arena building the world's frontier open deep-research model. Miners fine-tune the reigning king (genesis: Tongyi-DeepResearch-30B-A3B, a 30.5B MoE with ~3.3B active params) and submit challengers; validators run blind statistical duels on fresh research tasks. Beat the king at 99.9% confidence across a stake-weighted validator quorum and you hold the crown and roughly 90% of emissions.
hardwareRec: 1x consumer GPU is viable for serving/eval of the 3.3B-active MoE; fine-tuning challengers wants more VRAM (LoRA on 24GB feasible). Status badge says testnet-ready - confirm mainnet mechanics before committing spend.
keyRequirements: Fine-tune the current king and submit a digest-pinned Hugging Face checkpoint via timelock commit-reveal
Challenger must beat the king at 99.9% LCB over adaptive floor delta=0.05x(1-king accuracy), confirmed twice
Coronation requires accept verdicts covering >=51% of validator stake
Gates: config lock, size cap, 3 attempts per hotkey per round, one model per round, escalating loser cooldowns
Emissions: king 90% falling to 85%, arena (3 most recent ex-kings) 10% rising to 15%
A copy of the king mathematically cannot beat it by delta
minerJob: Miners are model trainers: fork/fine-tune the reigning king checkpoint, improve deep-research procedure quality (decompose, search, cross-check, attribute), upload a private digest-pinned checkpoint to HF, and commit through timelock commit-reveal so eval tasks are unknowable pre-reveal. Validators duel king vs challenger on ~1,000 fresh tasks (800 derived from the reveal's block hash, 200 from each validator's private pool). Winner-takes-most: ~90% of emissions to the crowned king, 10-15% to the three most recent ex-kings.
minerJobProvide: Digest-pinned challenger checkpoint (private unless crowned)
Measurable deep-research quality gain over the king
Compliant harness (config lock, size cap, no harness-breaking)
Fresh weights (copied weights are fingerprint-terminal)
Verified reward data produced as a duel byproduct
top10Strategy: Top-10 means being one of a handful of serious fine-tuners: mine the published headroom (base model scores 33.9% on Epago's exam; the 34-to-56 gap with perfect retrieval is the target; episodes die at turn/clock/context limits). Build a tight local eval loop mirroring the task style, train procedure skills, and submit only challengers that clear delta in your own testing - losing costs escalating cooldown time.
top10Levers: Fine-tuning skill on the 30B MoE base
Local eval harness mirroring duel task style
Attack episode completion failures (turn/clock/context)
Clean passage of cheap CPU intake gates
Iteration cadence faster than loser cooldowns reset
followTopMiners: Track the Epago dashboard (docs/DASHBOARD.md) for the current crown and reign age, taostats.io/subnet/36 weight concentration, and repo/docs updates - status is testnet-ready, so mechanism changes land in the repo first.

whatItDoes: TurboVision (Score) is a decentralized intelligence layer for live video and imagery, focused on professional sports. Validators run scoring jobs per Element from a manifest - building ground truth (real or SAM3 pseudo-GT), calling eligible miners' models from the on-chain registry, and paying per-Element winners. Sports and media buyers get structured, decision-ready data from raw footage.
hardwareRec: Per platform data: 1x GPU with >=16GB VRAM; RTX 5090, B200, H200, H20, MI300X explicitly excluded - plan 4090/A6000/L40S-class hardware. Workload is computer-vision model serving on video.
keyRequirements: Contribute models that solve Elements in the active Manifest
Hugging Face account with write access (HUGGINGFACE_USERNAME/API_KEY required)
Chutes developer account and CHUTES_API_KEY required
Validators call eligible miners from the on-chain registry and score outputs on live data
Per-element weight share; winners chosen over each element's eval_window (days)
Bittensor hotkey folder copied onto every host running TurboVision
minerJob: Miners publish and serve vision models addressing the Manifest's Elements (detection/tracking-style tasks on sports footage). The validator runner executes scoring jobs on a fixed block cadence (default 300 blocks per element): it fetches a challenge, builds ground truth, calls eligible registered miners, scores outputs, and emits shards to R2; aggregated per-Element scores pick winners whose weight share is normalized and set on-chain. MINER.md was 404 at research time, so follow repo docs and Score's channels for the exact miner contract.
minerJobProvide: Vision model endpoints solving Manifest Elements
Accurate predictions on live video/imagery windows
Reliable availability at each element's block cadence
HF-hosted model artifacts with pinned versions
Consistent scores across eval windows
top10Strategy: Score is per-Element winner-take-share: pick Elements where competition is thin and accuracy against the validator's ground-truth pipeline (real GT or SAM3 pseudo-GT) is achievable. Optimize for the actual scoring windows - 300-block cadence, eval_window lookbacks - not generic benchmarks. A newcomer wins by shipping one high-accuracy Element fast and then iterating on the pseudo-GT edge cases validators actually measure.
top10Levers: Element selection (thin-competition targets first)
Accuracy against SAM3 pseudo-GT quirks
Low-latency, always-on model endpoints
Fast response to manifest updates
Clean Chutes/HF integration (no scoring gaps)
followTopMiners: Track taostats.io/subnet/44 weight holders, Manifest updates in the repo (elements, weights, blacklist file), and winner snapshots emitted on every set_weights; watch wearescore.com and Score's channels for manifest changes.

whatItDoes: Synth (Mode Network) pays miners for synthetic price data: ensembles of 1,000 simulated price paths for crypto, equities, and commodities across 24h and 1h horizons. Validators score ensembles with CRPS against real price moves; emissions split equally across three competitions (Crypto 1h, Crypto 24h, Commodities/Equities 24h). AI agents, options traders, and portfolio managers consume the distributions.
hardwareRec: CPU only - path generation is numerical code (reference synth/miner/price_simulation.py). A modest VPS works; response latency matters because predictions are due before start_time and misses get the 90th-percentile penalty.
keyRequirements: Return 1,000 paths before start_time; invalid or late submissions score the 90th-percentile penalty
Three competitions with equal emission thirds: Crypto 1h (5-min increments, beta 0.3), Crypto 24h, Commodities/Equities 24h
Match the validator's price feed: Binance spot for BTC/ETH/SOL/XRP, Hyperliquid for the rest
Capture volatility clustering and fat-tailed distributions
Rolling average windows: 5 days (1h) and 10 days (24h); softmax allocation on relative rank
minerJob: Run an always-on daemon answering validator requests every ~15-32 minutes per asset: given (start_time, asset, time_increment, time_horizon, num_simulations), fetch the live price from the same feed the validator scores against, generate 1,000 correlated price paths (calibrated stochastic-vol models capturing volatility clustering and fat tails), and return them before start_time. Per-prompt CRPS scores roll into 5/10-day windows and emissions flow through a softmax on relative rank - small CRPS wins move big emission shares.
minerJobProvide: 1,000-path probabilistic forecasts per request, on time
Calibrated distributions competitive on CRPS
Realistic dynamics: volatility clustering, fat tails
Feed-matched spot prices at t0
Continuous availability across 13 assets and 3 competitions
top10Strategy: A quant research grind on a CPU base: build a proper stochastic-volatility/correlation simulator, calibrate continuously to the exact feeds, and never miss a deadline - the 90th-percentile penalty is brutal. The softmax is sharpest at beta 0.3 in Crypto 1h, where small calibration wins move large emission shares. Newcomers break top-10 by out-calibrating incumbents on one competition first, then expanding to the others.
top10Levers: Calibrated stochastic-volatility simulation code
Feed parity with the validator (Binance/Hyperliquid at t0)
Deadline reliability (penalty avoidance)
Competition selection (beta 0.3 Crypto 1h is sharpest)
Daily backtesting against realized moves
followTopMiners: Track taostats.io/subnet/50 CRPS-ranked UIDs and emission shares, the asset-change table in the README (feeds migrate, assets added often), and the Synth Discord for parameter changes.

whatItDoes: G.O.D (Gradients on Demand) runs recurring training tournaments: miners submit open-source training code (repo plus exact commit); the validator runs that code on its own GPU trainers, evaluates the resulting models, and advances winners through rounds. Consumers get trained models, and winning repositories are published open-source at gradients-opensource.
hardwareRec: CPU only for the miner itself - training executes on validator-controlled GPU trainer infrastructure. You need a dev box to write/test training code plus 0.4-0.7 TAO entry fees per tournament.
keyRequirements: Submit a training repo plus exact commit; the validator validates then runs it on dedicated trainers
Entry fees: Environment 0.6 TAO, Text 0.7 TAO, Image 0.4 TAO
Weekly windows Monday 09:00/11:00/13:00 UTC (Environment/Text/Image); minimum 4-5 miners to activate
Group, knockout/final, and boss/champion rounds; PvP evaluation for Environment tournaments
Code must be open-source; winning repos are published to gradients-opensource
Tournament performance feeds validator weight setting
minerJob: The miner exposes training repositories for tournament tasks. Each week you prepare training code for the task family (instruct/chat/DPO/GRPO for Text, diffusion for Image, environment/PvP for Environment), submit the repo and commit when a tournament opens, pay the fee, and wait while validator-side trainers execute the code and evaluate outputs through rounds. Your between-tournament job is iterating on training code based on last round's evaluations. Weights come from tournament outcomes, not uptime or hardware.
minerJobProvide: Open-source training code per tournament task family
Validated repo+commit that trains successfully on validator trainers
Models that win evaluation rounds
Round-over-round iterative improvements
Entry fee paid per tournament entered
top10Strategy: You compete on training-code quality, evaluated blind on validator GPUs - so maximize what generalizes: robust hyperparameters, clean data pipelines, proven recipes (GRPO/DPO variants) that do not overfit one task. Track the api.gradients.io tournament endpoints and study prior winning repos on gradients-opensource to see what wins. Newcomers can place by entering consistently - minimum-miner thresholds mean tournaments sometimes barely fill.

Code robustness on unknown validator hardware
Studying winning repos at gradients-opensource
Consistent weekly entry with budgeted fees
Round-format awareness (boss/champion rounds)
followTopMiners: Watch api.gradients.io/v1/tournaments/active and /latest/details for winners, the gradients-opensource org for winning code, taostats.io/subnet/56 weight distribution, and the repo's docs/miner.md guide.

whatItDoes: Chutes is Bittensor's serverless AI inference marketplace: miners operate GPU worker nodes that run community-deployed 'chutes' (vLLM/Python apps) and earn from real user inference traffic plus subnet emissions. It is the largest consumer-facing inference network; earnings scale with hardware size, uptime, and served demand.
hardwareRec: 8x H200-class node per platform data. Hard rules: bare metal/dedicated only (no Runpod/Vast), Intel TDX-capable CPUs with TEE via sek8s host-tools, unique static IP with 1:1 port mapping, RAM >= VRAM per GPU. Rental marketplaces banned.

Unique static IPs with 1:1 port mapping; no shared or dynamic IPs
RAM >= VRAM per GPU; TDX-capable Intel CPUs required
Miner software at rayonlabs/chutes-miner; GraVal GPU verification middleware
Legacy GraVal-only verification no longer supported - TDX enforced

The node pulls and serves chute images (vLLM-based model apps), handles encrypted inference traffic routed by the chutes API, and passes periodic hardware/TEE verification. Income comes from actual per-token inference revenue distributed on top of Yuma emissions - idle nodes earn little, so served demand and model coverage matter as much as raw specs.

Served user inference across deployed chutes
High uptime with static-IP reachability

Entry cost is high - dedicated TDX-capable servers - so model break-even against per-token rates at api.chutes.ai/pricing before buying. Newcomers rarely beat established fleets on price; target underserved models or regions instead.

TDX-capable dedicated hardware at competitive $/GPU-hour
Uptime and fast chute cold-starts
Model coverage aligned with demand
Staying current with sek8s/TEE tooling releases

whatItDoes: Leadpoet is an AI sales-intelligence competition: miners improve an open-source sales-research agent that finds companies matching hidden ICPs with verifiable intent evidence. whatItDoes: UMI (Umi-BitSign) builds ASL-to-English translation on Bittensor via endpoint competition and public model contributions. Endpoint miners serve translation models (may stay private); contributors submit licensed models for promotion into public baselines. Today a temporary bridge pays equal weights to registered miners passing HTTPS health checks - translation scoring is not yet the reward path.

System-trusted TLS certificate valid for the announced IP (self-signed or hostname-only rejected)
UID must have no validator permit; UID 0 and owner-associated hotkeys excluded

whatItDoes: Taostatus sources working LLM API access from miners for the BT Arena Protocol's AI agent pipeline. A miner's entire job: keep one working LLM credential (e.g. GPT-4o) available and hand it over encrypted when polled. Rewards track reliability, latency, volume, and model tier. NOTE: README states netuid 501 (testnet) - verify mainnet status before registering.

whatItDoes: Astrid (subnet 127) runs trading competitions on its Arena platform: miners trade, validators independently replay every trade to compute PnL rankings, and on-chain weights pay the top-3 of each completed competition 60/30/10 of that competition's emission share (the rest burns). This repo is the validator daemon only; miners participate via the Astrid Arena (arena-api.astrid.global).
